page.layout: One column of running text, set in italic verse, with a marginal note at the right edge of the lowest line. Running head at top centre. Page number at top left. Below the text a catchword at the right.

main_text.p:
Humanas elegis folicitudines,
Et vitæ fragilis præcipites fugas
Decantat querulo carmine clarior.
Illi Musa dedit pungere acumine
Mordaci vitium pectoribus latens,
Argutisque iocis & sale carpere
Corruptos hominum praua sequentium
Mores, atque vagæ damna licentiæ.
Et si quem placido lumine respicit
Phœbus, dat Cithara nectareum decus
Blandæ: qua cecinit Stesichorus grauis,
Alcæusque minax, & Rhodopeius
Orpheus: quam facili pollice Anacreon
Pulsauit teneris fœdus amoribus.
Olim quam Latiis attulit auribus,
Princepsque Æolium carmen ad Italos
Deduxit numeros Flaccus amabilis.
Sunt qui Graiugenis carmina vocibus
Scribunt: asl aly Romulidas fonis
Mulcent Ausonijs: Musaque vatibus
Gallis dat patria ludere tibia:
Paucis illa simul dona benignior
Mittit, si Charites tergemina fauent,
Et Phœbus Cithara si pater annuit.
Sic Beζam triplices ferre suum iubet
Lauros, sic variis ornat honoribus
Doctum Cacropio psallere pectine:
Doctum Romuleo pangere barbito.

page.notes: Verse set in italic lines; each line is printed as one line, rendered here with line breaks inside a paragraph. The marginal note "Anacreon" stands at the right beside the line "Orpheus: quam facili pollice" (the printed mark ⸻ in the margin). The word "Et" at the bottom right is a catchword/signature-like fragment set in the right margin, in roman type. The Greek-letter-free text is all Latin. Doubtful: "Beζam" is a misreading of the printed name, which appears to be "Bezam" with a long-s-like form; "asl" likely "ast" (= at); "Mulcent Ausonijs" likely "Ausonijs" printed as "Ausonijs". Marginal mark "Ζ" is not reliable; "Be[?]am" should be read as the printed name. Some accents over vowels in "Æolium", "Cithara" are printed macron/tilde variants.
